introduction_markdown: CAMEROON GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. 0520 COMMERCE 1, JUNE 2020, ORDINARY / INTERMEDIATE LEVELS. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. Calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is appropriate, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet, using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

questions.enonce_markdown: Home trade is usually sub-divided into;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trade carried on inside a country is called home (domestic) trade. It is divided into **wholesale trade** (buying goods in large quantities from producers and selling them in smaller quantities to retailers) and **retail trade** (selling goods in small quantities to the final consumers). Import and export trade belong to foreign trade, so options A, B and D are wrong because each mixes home trade with foreign trade.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Whole sale trade and export trade.
Whole sale trade and retail trade.

questions.enonce_markdown: A partner who does not take part in the sharing of profits in a partnership business is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **nominal partner** lends his or her name to the firm (to give it prestige or credit) but contributes no capital and receives no share of the profits. A quasi partner is a former or deceased partner whose share stays in the business as a loan, an active partner takes part in running the business and shares profits, and a limited partner invests capital and does share profits but cannot manage the business.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document that permits a public limited company to start business is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When a company is registered, the Registrar issues a certificate of incorporation, and the company then exists as a legal person. A **private** company may start business at once with this certificate. A **public** limited company, however, must first raise its share capital from the public and then obtain a **certificate of trading** before it is allowed to start business. The memorandum and the articles of association are documents filed to apply for registration, they do not give the right to trade.

Note the link with question 46: certificate of incorporation for a private company, certificate of trading for a public company.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The importation of goods for re-export is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Entrepôt trade** (re-export trade) means importing goods into a country in order to export them again, usually after storing, packing or sorting them in a bonded warehouse. Foreign trade is the general name for all trade between countries, import trade is only buying from abroad, and export trade is only selling abroad.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A clerk employed by a bank can be classified under which of the following;

*Options as printed:* A) Industry.   B) Direct services.   C) Commerce.   D) Tertiary industry.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bank is an **aid to trade**: it provides banking services (accounts, loans, payments) that help commerce. The clerk who works there therefore belongs to the commerce group of activities, and not to industry (which makes goods). However, "tertiary industry" (commerce plus direct services) and "direct services" can also be defended, so the printed question is ambiguous.

**Intended answer: C (Commerce).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: An advertisement directed to the general public is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Indirect advertising** is aimed at the general public at large, through mass media such as television, radio, newspapers and posters, without choosing a particular group of buyers. **Direct advertising** is aimed at a chosen person or market segment (for example a letter or leaflet sent to selected customers), as in question 32. Informative and persuasive describe the purpose of the advert, not who receives it.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following risks are insurable EXCEPT;

*Options as printed:* A) Loss caused by natural disaster.   B) Loss caused by civil unrest.   C) Fidelity guarantee.   D) Burglary.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Burglary (theft) and fidelity guarantee (dishonesty of employees) are standard insurable risks: the event is accidental, the loss can be measured in money and the insured has an insurable interest. Losses caused by civil unrest (riots, war-like disorder) and by some natural disasters are often excluded from ordinary policies or insured only by special extension, so either A or B could be the intended exception. The printed question does not allow a safe choice.

**Intended answer: B (Loss caused by civil unrest).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are features of commercial banks EXCEPT;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Commercial banks are limited liability companies that aim at making profit, and they take part in the money market by lending and borrowing short-term funds. **Regulating other banks** (supervising them and controlling credit) is a function of the central bank, not of a commercial bank.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Profits maximization is their main objective.
They form part of the money market.

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest advantage of sea transport over other forms of transport is that it is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Sea transport can carry very large quantities of bulky goods over long distances at a low cost per tonne, so it is the **cheapest** form of transport. It is slow (not faster than air transport) and not flexible, since ships use only fixed ports.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A retail outlet with no display room but relies on catalogues to sell goods is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **mail order business** sells through catalogues, advertisements and the post (or delivery service): the customer orders from the catalogue and the goods are sent to the home, so no shop display is needed. A mobile shop sells from a vehicle that moves around, and an independent trader owns a normal shop.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the rate of VAT is 10%, and the cost price of goods is 500,000 CFAF, determine VAT amount:
questions.corrige_markdown:
VAT amount = rate × cost price = $\dfrac{10}{100} \times 500\,000 = 50\,000$ CFAF.

Option B comes from taking 1% instead of 10%, C and D come from subtracting the VAT from the price instead of finding the VAT itself.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A crossed cheque with the name of the bank between the parallel lines refers to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque crossed with two parallel lines and the **name of a bank** written between them is a **special crossing**: the cheque must be paid into an account at that named bank. With a general crossing there are only the two parallel lines (perhaps with "& Co." or "not negotiable"), so it can be paid into any bank account.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Gross profits less expenses is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Gross profit is the difference between sales and cost of goods sold. When the running **expenses** (rent, wages, transport, etc.) are deducted from it, what remains is the **net profit**.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An advertising medium that has limited information is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **poster** is read quickly by people passing by, so it can carry only a few words, a picture and a slogan. Magazines can give long and detailed information, and television and radio give more time to explain the product. (Radio also has a short message, but a poster is the usual textbook example of limited information.)

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The sale of goods unfit for consumption is prevented by which of the following acts?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **Sale of Goods Act** protects the buyer by requiring goods to match their description and to be of satisfactory (merchantable) quality and fit for the purpose for which they are sold. Goods unfit for consumption break these conditions, so the buyer can reject them and claim damages. A consumer credit act deals with loans and hire purchase, and the other two options do not deal with the quality of goods.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A bank facility that enables customers to deposit money after closing hours is called;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **night safe** is a secure chute in the wall of the bank: a trader puts the day's takings in a locked wallet and drops it in after closing time. The bank opens it the next day and credits the account. An ATM or cash dispenser gives money out, and a franking machine is an office machine for stamping mail.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mail service that the pays full compensation for missing item is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
With **registered post** the item is recorded at every stage and the sender receives a certificate of posting, and compensation is paid if the item is lost or damaged, up to the value declared and insured. Express delivery is mainly a faster service, and recorded delivery only proves that the item was delivered. The wording "full compensation" is not precise, so this key rests on the usual textbook answer.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The difference between visible exports and visible imports is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Visible items are goods that can be seen and counted. The value of visible exports minus the value of visible imports is the **balance of trade** (a surplus if exports are larger, a deficit if imports are larger). The balance of payments is wider, because it also includes invisible items (services) and capital movements, and the terms of trade compare export prices with import prices.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The amount paid for space not used in a ship is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Dead freight** is the compensation paid by a shipper to the shipowner when he books space on a ship but does not use it all. Demurrage is a charge for keeping the ship in port longer than the agreed time, chartered freight is the price paid to hire the ship, and dock dues are port charges.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Enterprises can be classified according to the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Enterprises are classified by their **activity** (primary, secondary, tertiary), by their **size** (small, medium, large) and by their **ownership** (private, public, mixed). "Production" is one of the activities carried out by enterprises, it is not a basis for classifying them, so it is the exception.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An accepted bill of exchange entitles the creditor to do the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bill of exchange is an order written by the creditor (drawer) telling the debtor (drawee) to pay a sum on a fixed date. Once the debtor has accepted (signed) it, the creditor can keep it until it matures, **endorse** it to a third party to settle his own debts, or discount it at a bank. The **promise to pay** is made by the debtor when he accepts the bill, not by the creditor, so it is the exception.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Endorse it to a third party.
Keep it till date of maturity.

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used when a hired means of transport is used is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **consignment note** is made out when goods are handed to a carrier (a transport firm hired by the trader). It describes the goods, the sender and the receiver and is the contract and the proof of dispatch. An advice note informs the buyer that goods have been sent, and a delivery note goes with the goods to be signed by the receiver.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An enterprise whose capital ranges between 50 and 500 millions CFAF in Cameroon is said to have:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the size classification used at this level, small enterprises have a small capital (below 50 million CFAF), **medium** enterprises have a capital between 50 and 500 million CFAF and large enterprises have more than 500 million CFAF. "Normal" is not a size category. The exact limits are those of the textbook, not an official text checked for this correction.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Foreign trade is sub-divided into;

*Options as printed:* A) Import and Export.   B) Wholesale trade and export trade.   C) Export trade and import trade.   D) Enterpot Trade and import.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Foreign trade (trade between countries) is divided into **import trade** (buying from abroad), **export trade** (selling abroad) and entrepôt trade (re-export). Options A and C both say "import and export" in a different order, so two options are correct and the printed question is defective.

**Intended answer: A (Import and Export).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The retail shop whose section are controlled by "buyers" is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **department store** is a large shop divided into departments (clothes, furniture, electrical goods...), and each department is run by a specialist "buyer" who chooses the goods and is responsible for its results. Multiple shops are chains of similar branches, and supermarkets and hypermarkets are self-service shops.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The abbreviation 'E&O.E' refers to:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**E. & O.E.** means "Errors and Omissions Excepted". It is printed at the bottom of an invoice or statement to say that the seller keeps the right to correct any mistake or omission in it afterwards.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these facilities below enable bank customers to withdraw money from their accounts at any time?
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **Automatic Teller Machine (ATM)** works day and night, so a customer with a card can take money out at any time. A cheque can only be cashed during banking hours, and standing orders and direct debits are instructions for paying regular amounts to someone else, not for withdrawing cash.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Telefax means;
questions.corrige_markdown:
"Fax" is the short form of **facsimile** (an exact copy). Telefax is a communication service that sends a copy of a document over the telephone line. Only option C has the correct spelling, the other three are misspelled.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When an insurer transfers part of a risk to another insurance company. It is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Re-insurance** means that an insurer who has accepted a big risk passes part of it to another insurance company, so that a very large loss is shared. Surrender value is paid on a life policy that is cancelled, and contribution is the sharing of a loss between insurers when the same risk is insured with several (options B and D are the same word).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One reason why Cameroon is involved in foreign trade;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Countries do not have the same climate, soil, minerals and other natural resources, so no country can produce everything it needs. Cameroon trades abroad to obtain goods that it lacks or produces at a high cost (for example machines or oil products) and sells goods that it has in surplus (for example cocoa, coffee or timber). Peace, debts and a surplus are possible effects, not the basic reason.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Due to differences in natural endowment.
Ensure a balance of payments surplus.

questions.enonce_markdown: The document issued to show a summary of trade transactions for a month is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the end of the month the seller sends the buyer a **statement of account**. It lists the invoices, credit notes and payments of the month and shows the balance still to be paid. An invoice covers a single sale, a credit note corrects an invoice in the buyer's favour, and a promissory note is a written promise to pay.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An advert that targets a particular market segment is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Direct advertising** is aimed at a chosen group or segment of the market (for example a leaflet for farmers about fertilisers, or a letter to existing customers). Indirect advertising addresses the general public. Informative and persuasive describe what the advert tries to do.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a hire purchase transaction the buyer must pay what fraction of price to make repossession impossible?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In hire purchase the goods belong to the seller until all instalments are paid, so the seller may take them back if the buyer defaults. By the **one-third rule** taught in commerce, once the buyer has paid **one third** of the hire purchase price, the goods can no longer be taken back without a court order. The fractions 2/3, 1/2 and 3/4 are larger than the rule requires.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cost of goods sold ÷ average stock equals:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **rate of stock turnover** shows how many times the average stock is sold and replaced in a period:

$$\text{rate of stock turnover}=\frac{\text{cost of goods sold}}{\text{average stock}}$$

"Turnover" (option D) means the total value of sales, which is a different idea, and margin is profit as a percentage of sales.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An agent that take possession of goods and sells in his own name is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **factor** is a mercantile agent who is given the goods (possession) by the owner and sells them in his own name, receiving a commission. A broker never holds the goods, a del credere agent guarantees that the buyers will pay, and a forwarding agent arranges transport.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cheque NOT presented for payment for more than six months is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque which is not presented to the bank within **six months** of its date is a **stale cheque**, and the bank will normally refuse to pay it. A post-dated cheque carries a future date, a dishonoured cheque is refused by the bank (for example for lack of funds) and an endorsed cheque has been signed over to another person.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A form of advert used by a firm to launch a new product is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When a new product is launched, the public does not yet know it, so the firm uses **informative advertising** to tell people what the product is, what it does, its price and where to buy it. Persuasive and competitive adverts are used later, to convince buyers to prefer the product to others.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The only document below which is used in foreign trade is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **consular invoice** is an invoice certified by the consul of the importing country in the exporter's country, and it is used only in foreign trade (for customs control and to prove the value and origin of the goods). A credit sales invoice and a promissory note are used in home trade as well, and a pro forma invoice can also be used as a quotation in home trade.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A transportation means that links other transport systems is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Road transport** can reach almost any place, so it collects goods from farms, factories and shops and carries them to railway stations, ports and airports, and from them to the final customer. That is why it is the link between the other systems.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A foreign order to an agent to buy good from named manufacturer is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **indent** is an order sent from an importer to an agent in the exporting country. In a **closed indent** the importer names the manufacturer from whom the goods must be bought, and in an **open indent** the agent is free to choose the supplier. Because the manufacturer is named, the answer is the closed indent (option C is too general because every such order is an indent).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The greatest advantage of air transport over other forms of transport is that it is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Air transport is the **fastest** means of transport, which makes it ideal for urgent, perishable or valuable goods. It is expensive, it is not suited to heavy bulky goods and goods may need transshipment at airports.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The restriction on the importation of particular types of goods into a country is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **quota** limits the quantity of a particular good that may be imported in a period. Tariffs are taxes on imports (a price measure, not a restriction on quantity), and export subsidies help exporters. An embargo is a complete ban, usually on trade with a given country, so it could also be argued; the key rests on the word "restriction".

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A licensed agent that sell goods to the highest bidder is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **auctioneer** is a licensed agent who sells goods in public by inviting bids, and the goods go to the highest bidder. He is paid a commission by the owner of the goods.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The profits made by a businessman that sells goods for 200,000 CFAF at a margin of 25% is worth:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **margin** is profit expressed as a percentage of the **selling price**:

$$\text{profit}=\frac{25}{100}\times 200\,000 = 50\,000 \text{ CFAF}$$

Check: cost price = 200,000 - 50,000 = 150,000 CFAF. The trap is option B (40,000), which is 25% of the cost price (a mark-up on cost would give $200\,000 \times 25/125 = 40\,000$).

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A rebate given to the retailer by the wholesaler to enable him make profits is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **trade discount** is a reduction from the list price that a wholesaler gives to a retailer, so that the retailer can resell at the list price and make a profit. A cash discount is given for quick payment, and a mark-up is added by the seller to the cost price.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The document required by a private company to start business is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **private company** can begin trading as soon as it has received its **certificate of incorporation**, which proves that it has been registered and exists as a legal person. A public company needs in addition a certificate of trading (question 3). The memorandum and the articles of association are the documents sent to the Registrar to apply for registration.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An insurance principle that allows a company to take over the scrap value after full compensation is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
By the principle of **subrogation**, when the insurer has paid the insured in full for a loss, it takes over the rights of the insured on what is left (the scrap or salvage of a damaged car, for instance) and on any claim against the person who caused the loss. Indemnity means that the insured is put back in the same position and not made richer, and contribution is the sharing of a loss between insurers.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The amount paid to an insured who discontinues payment of premium in life insurance policy is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A life policy builds up a cash value. If the insured stops paying the premiums, the insurer pays him the **surrender value** (a part of the premiums already paid) and the policy ends. A premium is the price of the insurance, an annuity is a yearly payment for life or a fixed period, and indemnity applies to loss insurance.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Shop lifting is NOT common with which of the following types of retail shops?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Shoplifting (stealing goods from the shelves) happens where customers walk among displayed goods, as in department stores and hypermarkets. A **mail order** business has no shop floor, because customers order from a catalogue and the goods are sent to them, so shoplifting is not a problem there.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A deceased or retired partner whose share of capital is retained in the business as a loan is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **quasi partner** is a person who has left the partnership (by retirement or death) but whose share of capital stays in the firm as a loan. He is not a partner any more, but he may receive interest or a share of profits on the loan.

**Answer: B.**
